key_insight: Linearizing the Boltzmann equation with its full collision operator reproduces classical incompressible shear-flow stability and transient-growth results within a unified kinetic framework.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables consistent comparison of full and simplified collision models for predicting disturbance amplification and instability in canonical shear flows.
method: Discretize the full hard-sphere, BGK, ES-BGK and Shakhov operators within one energy-stable formulation.
Combine fast spectral collision evaluation with matrix-free, preconditioned shift-invert Arnoldi solves.
Compute modal stability, transient growth and pseudospectra using a kinetic disturbance-energy norm.
evidence_signal: Across four canonical flows at Reynolds numbers 10²–10⁵, reported eigenvalue agreement is within a few parts in 10⁷ for relaxation models and 10⁶ for the full operator, with transient growth and resolvent norms reproduced to 0.1%.
watch_item: The four-dimensional kinetic discretization remains computationally demanding, and ill-conditioned eigenvalues may not converge even when pseudospectra do.
paper_title: Kinetic linear stability theory for incompressible parallel shear flows with the full Boltzmann collision operator
